basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Ab hoc exivit proverbium: Quasi Nemrod robustus venator coram Domino. Ideo in proverbium'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Ab hoc exivit proverbium: Quasi Nemrod robustus venator coram Domino. Ideo in proverbium versa, quia insolita saeculis ejus facta fuere; quod vero additur coram Domino, exaggerandi facinoris causa est, quia videlicet satis temerarium fuerit et superbum, ut coram Domino, qui de coelo prospicit super filios hominum, taliter vivere homo in terra praesumeret; ex quo nimirum proverbio patet quia multi tempore illo fuere qui talia facere metu superni respectus vitabant, quamvis alia Editio habet quia Nemrod gigans venator contra Dominum. Ex ambiguo quippe Graeco, quod est enantion, utrumque potest interpretari. Denique in psalmo ubi canimus ploremus coram Domino qui fecit nos (Psal. CIV, 6), hoc verbum est enantion Cyrium. Hoc et in libro Job, ubi scriptum est, in furorem erupisti contra Dominum. Facilis ergo patet intellectus de gigante, quia robustus fuerit venator brutorum animalium, quasi homo potens; sed quia homo impius contra voluntatem Conditoris vitam duxerit superbam.
